Brian's pack list is where it starts. Robert's picks for the board and the zombies stand unless he's changed them since. {"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# ZM3D playable: hand-off notes

The brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.

The hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.

State is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.

Brian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.

Sound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.

Tickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.

Sharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.
", "id": "f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008", "name": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes"}

• Blunder was fine the way it is, but it got skewed because of these recent weird bot like behavior.
• Win rate still has more impact on funnel, blunder seems to be OK as long as people win.
• We are leaning more hardcore because casual doesn't cut it, or so we think
• We support this hardcore transition with level templates and monster scaling using a math formula
• We differentiate our game with the zombie killing + card mechanic

This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass - Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

ZM3D has not had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray - the primary tempo penalty, not the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families - cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

The roster is an everyday-people theme rather than classic undead. Minion families scale in tiers; bosses come in standard, Fast and Turbo variants.

FamilyTypeTiers
PunkMinion1-5
BikerMinion1-4
KarenMinion1-4
AfroMinion1-3
Riot Police, Chef, Scientist, Fire Fighter, Magician, Librarian, Tech Bro, Gym Bro, Baseball Player, CheerleaderMinionin development
VarC-Mayor1 250 / VarC-Mayor2 225 / VarC-Chef 175 (base HP, scaled at runtime; the older 180/300/500 prefabs are retired)Bossstandard, Fast, Turbo

Elemental weaknesses used by boosters and abilities: shock, poison, burn, freeze, splash, stun, blind. Glue is a booster, not an element.

Modes

  • Campaign - authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless - survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss - a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc - do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash from consecutive glass-impact SFX/VFX on Android, mostly Samsung (Aug-Sep 2025, ZOM-475), fixed by removing the glass SFX and VFX. The separate addressables splash-hang belongs to Domino Delights.
  • The font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections is also Domino Delights (ENG-2346, May 2025); the ZM3D client has no remote font download.

Boss mode reward config

Owner: Robert (Product). Design: Julia Lawson. Changes to tray count or refill cadence must be reviewed against the OKR dashboard before shipping.

It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. ZM3D has not had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1757695108.506159\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, the way I see it, playables can be good for optimizing for CPIs (fun casual playable but unrelated to core game), optimizing for retention (filter out users that are not going to like your game), or somewhere in the middle. {"ts": "1758911910.876289", "type": "message", "text": "I’ve been playing Archero 2 and <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io> for a while, and I’ve developed some theories about how levels and monsters work in these games
• In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.
    ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength.
• In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player\u2019s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you\u2019re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.\n    \u25e6 Another thing I\u2019m confident about is that the monsters\u2019 HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you\u2019re suddenly dealing with 100. input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (Harmony Games). Written 1 October 2025 by Julia Lawson, for the build start on 3 November 2025.

This brief describes the game as it is today. We are reviewing the core gameplay during the pause. If the core changes, we will redo the affected part of this brief with you in November.

1. Scenario
We picked Scenario 1: the core-mechanic playable, showing the basic gameplay in its simplest and most authentic form.
What it is for: we are optimising for player quality and retention, not cheap installs. The playable should filter out people who won't enjoy the real game, while staying true to it, so first tests give clean, reliable results.
How it plays: the player can pick any items freely and make as many matches as they are good enough to make. It is not on rails like the Domino Delights playable.
Build it as the board-editable version you offered: the eight items below are the default board, and we can swap in extras to test. Keeping control over how many zombies and items are on the board is useful to us.

2. Board items
The default board is these eight items:
- Grenade (Survival)
- Couch (Living Room)
- Plushie Chick (Toys) - the item you called "the duck" in the reference level
- Shuriken (Survival)
- Cute Axe (Survival)
- Gift Box (Toys)
- Cactus Plant (Garden) - new colour versions are coming, see the hand-off list
- Bow (Toys) - as it is now, without an arrow
Every other board item on the hand-off list is an extra you can swap in. That includes Couch and Pillow and Plushie Bunny from the reference level, and Dynamite, which was on an earlier version of the list.
Weapon: the Cannon, which is what you've been calling the rocket launcher, sent with its projectile in the first zip on 24 September.
Background: the background from the reference level, sent in the first zip on 24 September.

3. Zombies and animation
Use these four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player.
Use one animation: walk.
All four are in the Unity package Brian sent on 26 September, so you can re-rig them in Spine from that. We can add more zombies later if size and scope allow.

4. Winning and losing
The board is a physics pile of 3D items. The player drags items into a tray that has 7 slots. Any 3 matching items in the tray clear, and each cleared match fires that item at the zombies.
Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
Lose: the zombies reach the player and the player's HP runs out. The loss screen only appears at zero HP.
A full tray is not a loss: if all 7 slots fill without a match, the tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage (they get tougher), but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state.
Different items hit zombies differently: for example the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage, and the plushie is weak but funny.
The reference level we built on 23 September, which Brian recorded and sent you on 24 September, shows all of this.

5. Sound
You can use these now; they are ours to hand over:
- Matching sound
- Success sound
- Failure sound
Still to come from us:
- Background music: a new track made for the ad (not the in-game track), being cut down to a loop.
- Rocket sound and explosion sound: the current ones come from a sound library and a bought sound pack. They stay with us until we have our own versions, so please don't use the sounds from the game build. We will send our own versions.
Music: as you told us last time, music may only start after the player's first tap or click.

6. Formats
Your format list from September still applies:
- 3D: .fbx, .glb or .blend. FBX files must be exported as Binary, not ASCII.
- 2D: .png. For 2D animations, character parts must be separated into pieces.
- Fonts: .ttf or .woff2.
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav.

7. Start date
The build starts on Monday 3 November 2025, with the kickoff call that day.

8. What's still coming from us
The hand-off list (a separate sheet, linked in the PlayableX channel) has one row per asset. Each row shows its state:
- Delivered: you have the current file.
- Ready: exported and waiting in our outgoing folder.
- Owed: still with us, with what's owed and who has it.
As of 1 October: 8 Delivered, 68 Ready, 20 Owed.
Of the eight default board items, only the Cactus Plant is still owed, because of its new colour versions. Grenade, Couch and Plushie Chick are delivered. Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box and Bow are ready.

Done. Here's where the pack stands across Brian's 96 lines:
• *Delivered:* 8
• *Ready:* 68
• *Owed:* 20

Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/99921598485200eaf6965d53/edit
Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YRCfn_GhVGI-bi6yKoxXFSABaPt8aJRIRRMFGHPQ5oI/edit
Both are view-only for you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake. The links are going in the PlayableX channel now.

Things worth knowing:
• *Board change:* Robert put the Bow in the eight instead of Dynamite (26 Sep, in #zombie-art). Dynamite is now an extra.
• *Board item still owed:* Cactus Plant is the only one of the eight not ready. Robert got new colour versions of the cactus, chainsaw and cone on 29 Sep, which is after Claire's FBXs were exported, so all three have to go again from Claire.
• *Zombies:* Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player, walk only. That's Robert's pick and it hasn't changed.
• *Sound:* rocket and explosion are from a library and a bought pack, so they stay here until Calvin makes our own. Calvin is also still cutting the music to a loop.
• *Owed by person:* Claire 9, Brian 7, Calvin 3, Martin 1 (fonts).
• *Tickets:* the 20 Owed ones are in Todo with a comment each. Delivered and Ready ones are untouched.

input.message:
Hi team, here's what you need for the ZM3D playable ahead of the 3 November start.

• *Brief* (scenario, the eight board items, the four zombies and the walk animation, win/lose and the 7-slot tray, sound, formats, start date): https://docs.google.com/document/d/99921598485200eaf6965d53/edit
• *Hand-off list* (one row per asset, with its state, what's still owed and who has it): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YRCfn_GhVGI-bi6yKoxXFSABaPt8aJRIRRMFGHPQ5oI/edit

Of 96 assets, 8 are already with you, 68 are exported and ready to send, and 20 are still coming from us. The 20 still coming are:
• Cactus Plant (one of the eight) plus Chainsaw and Cone, as new colour versions
• 8 more extra board items
• Item icons and UI as PNG
• Fonts
• The music loop
• Our own rocket and explosion sounds. Please don't use the ones from the game build.

The brief is written for the game as it is today. If the core gameplay changes during the pause, we'll redo that part with you in November.

content.text:
I've done everything in Frederick's Sep 30 message. The brief and the hand-off list are in your Drive, the tickets are updated, his counts are in his DM, and both links are in the PlayableX channel. One slip: my channel post said 8 extra board items are still owed when it's 11. I posted a correction in the thread; the total of 20 was right.

**The pack, across Brian's 96 lines (sent to Frederick):** 8 Delivered, 68 Ready, 20 Owed.

**What changed from Brian's notes:**
- **The board changed.** On Sep 26 Robert put the **Bow** in the eight instead of **Dynamite**. The eight are now Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant and Bow. Dynamite is an extra.
- **Three items need re-exporting.** On Sep 29 Robert said there are new colour versions of the **Cactus Plant, Chainsaw and Cone**. Brian had already exported all three, so they go again from Claire. Cactus is the only one of the eight not ready.
- **Two sounds stay with us.** Calvin's sound sources sheet shows the **rocket** sound is from a sound library and the **explosion** from a bought pack. Both are Owed until Calvin makes our own. The music is also Owed while Calvin cuts it to a loop.
- **The zombies are as Robert picked them:** Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player, walk animation only. Nothing has changed since.

**Who has the 20 Owed lines:** Claire 9, Brian 7, Calvin 3, Martin 1 (fonts).

**Files** (both view-only for Frederick, Brian, Robert and intake@playablex.ai, per Frederick's notes):
- [Brief for PlayableX](https://docs.google.com/document/d/99921598485200eaf6965d53/edit): written for the game as it is today. It covers what Frederick's notes ask for:
  - Scenario 1 and why we picked it
  - the eight board items, with everything else as extras
  - the zombies and walk animation
  - how a level is won and lost, and the 7-slot tray, where a full tray enrages the zombies but isn't a loss
  - which sounds they can use, and that music starts only after the first tap
  - their formats and the Nov 3 start
- [Hand-off list](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YRCfn_GhVGI-bi6yKoxXFSABaPt8aJRIRRMFGHPQ5oI/edit): one row per line, with the columns Frederick asked for.

**Tickets:** the 20 Owed tickets are moved to Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it. I didn't touch the Delivered and Ready tickets.

**Slack:** I replied in Frederick's DM thread and posted both links in the PlayableX channel.

I couldn't find the Dominoes playable brief anywhere, so I built this one from Frederick's hand-off notes. The rocket and explosion files Brian exported are still in the outgoing folder. Someone should keep them out of the next zip so they don't reach PlayableX by mistake.
